questions.q: What is Horizon Catalog, as described in this lesson?
options: Snowflake's built-in governance and discovery layer, which now actively enforces policy on agent and human queries at runtime
A third-party data catalog tool that connects to Snowflake
A replacement for GRANT and roles that removes the need for RBAC
A warehouse sizing recommendation engine
questions.explain: Horizon Catalog sits above the role/GRANT model from Chapter 9 and, by 2026, actively enforces masking, row access, and purpose-based controls at runtime, not just documents data after the fact.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Horizon's five governance pillars?
options: Performance
Security
Privacy
Compliance
questions.explain: The five pillars are Security, Privacy, Access, Compliance, and Interoperability. Performance tuning (Chapter 10) is a separate topic, not one of Horizon's pillars.

questions.q: What does setting auto_tag: true on a classification profile do?
options: Automatically applies recommended system tags to columns Snowflake classifies as sensitive
Automatically deletes any column containing PII
Automatically grants SELECT on every classified table to ACCOUNTADMIN
Automatically converts the table to a secure view
questions.explain: auto_tag controls whether Snowflake sets recommended classification system tags on columns it identifies as sensitive during automatic classification.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why did Horizon need to move from documenting data to enforcing policy at runtime?
options: Agents can run hundreds of chained, unattended queries in seconds — far faster than a catalog that only describes data after the fact can account for
Snowflake deprecated roles and GRANT entirely
Regulators require every Snowflake account to use Horizon by law
Row access policies and masking policies stopped working without Horizon
questions.explain: The volume and speed of agent-driven access outpaces what a passive, descriptive catalog can account for, which is why Horizon shifted to active, runtime policy enforcement.

questions.q: Which pillar covers governance extending to external engines reading Snowflake-managed data via the Iceberg REST Catalog?
options: Interoperability
Privacy
Access
Security
questions.explain: Interoperability is the pillar that extends Horizon's governance to external, Iceberg-compatible engines reading Snowflake-managed tables, not just native Snowflake queries.
